single_biggest_error: The mobile finding is a textbook Trap-1 failure and the lane broke the toolkit's own house rule to produce it. It declared "ARY's entire 'Mobile' product group is 8 SKUs, all of them chargers — no handsets, no accessories of substance" from ProductGroupID=139 alone, without running `ary assort probe`, which CLAUDE.md and Data-Quality-Traps.md both mandate before any "ARY does not carry X". Group 139 sold ₹2,690 in 12 months — it is a dead group, not the category. ARY's real mobile business sits in ProductGroupName 'Accessories', sub-groups Mobile Accessories / Earphone / Mobile Set: 15 SKUs, ₹1,98,119 in 12 months (Mobile Adapter ₹49,796, Mobile Datacable ₹47,607, Bluetooth Buds ₹46,543, Mobile Ear Phone ₹39,983, Airpod ₹5,594), plus a "Mobile Handset" SKU and an "Iphone 17 Pro Max 256Gb Silver" filed under Confectionery. The lane measured 1.3% of the category and called the other 98.7% absent. The consequence is not just an embarrassing citation: it makes the ₹55,000/month repair estimate look like greenfield when it is in fact 3.3x the entire existing mobile category's annual sales, and it hides that ARY already has a live accessory line and a supplier to bolt repair onto.

verdicts.claim: 18 named contract tailors on their own ledger group 'Stiching Charges Payable' (group 508)

verdicts.claim: Tailoring earned +₹45,511 on ₹15,79,023 of revenue = +2.9% GM over 3.4 years; FY26-27 to 21-Aug was +16.7%
verdicts.live_number: Like-for-like through 31-Jul-2026: +₹34,971 on ₹15,68,483 = +2.2%. FY26-27 Apr-Jul like-for-like: +₹39,667 = +13.7%
verdicts.query_used: Revenue: SELECT YEAR(DATEADD(month,-3,h.VoucherDate)) fy, SUM(d.FinalSaleAmount) FROM SaleDetail d JOIN SaleHeader h ... WHERE d.ProductID='07NL' GROUP BY fy. Cost: SELECT YEAR(DATEADD(month,-3,m.VoucherDate)) fy, SUM(c.DebitAmount) FROM TransactionChild c JOIN TransactionMaster m ... WHERE c.AccountID IN (2228,1922) AND m.IsDeleted=0 GROUP BY fy. Then the same two by FORMAT(date,'yyyy-MM')
verdicts.why: Every full-year figure reproduces to the rupee (FY23-24 ₹2,96,690/₹2,61,938; FY24-25 ₹4,34,416/₹4,22,540; FY25-26 ₹5,48,052/₹5,99,376 = -9.4%, all exact). But the totals are cut-off mismatched. The monthly breakdown shows the stitching cost is a single month-end accrual journal and the ledger's last one is 31-Jul-2026, while 07NL revenue accrues daily — so the lane compared 4.7 months of revenue against 4.0 months of cost. Trimming both to 31-Jul gives +2.2%, not +2.9%; the FY26-27 row falls from +16.7% to +13.7%, and on today's live data the same method would print a spurious +25.0%. The headline conclusion — tailoring is break-even, not a margin business — survives and is arguably strengthened. The year-by-year table does not: the pass-through ratio swings 88% → 97% → 109% → 86%, which is accrual timing noise, not a pricing policy.

verdicts.why: The lane's self-correction is right and it reported its own error rather than burying it. The expense genuinely lands on accounts 2228 'Stiching Charges' and 1922 'Stiching Exp.', both group 30 Direct Expenses, with the tailors' payable as the contra. Good discipline.

verdicts.claim: Stitching attaches to only 13.9% of the fabric ARY sells (187 of 1,341 bills)
verdicts.live_number: Arithmetic reproduces (FY26-27 to 30-Aug: 191/1,388 = 13.8%; live 12m: 314/2,713 = 11.6%; widened to all garment groups: 431/4,977 = 8.7%). But by counter: Ary Clothing 313/1,611 = 19.4%, Ary Pos 1/1,102 = 0.09%
verdicts.query_used: CTE over SaleHeader x SaleDetail x ProductMaster flagging MAX(CASE WHEN ProductGroupID IN (183,124,165)) and MAX(CASE WHEN ProductID='07NL') per SerialNumber, 2025-09-01 to 2026-09-01; then the same CTE grouped by WarehouseMaster.WarehouseName
verdicts.why: The number reproduces but the metric cannot measure what it claims, and the blend hides the actionable finding. First, 74% of stitching bills (443 of 734 in FY26-27) contain no fabric line at all — customers bring cloth back on a later visit, and with 96.3% of bills anonymous that link is unrecoverable, so same-bill co-occurrence is a floor, not an attach rate. Second, and more useful: the 13.9% is an average of a counter that runs 19.4% and a counter that runs 0.09%. Ary Pos sells ₹20.7 L/yr of fabric and unstitched suits and books 4 stitching lines a year. That is the concrete thing to fix, and the lane missed it despite building a warehouse-economics table in the very next finding.

verdicts.claim: Paytm/UPI is 56.3% of all tender lines and 42.9% of value in FY26-27
verdicts.live_number: Tender share 56.3% CONFIRMED (103,070 of 182,995). Value share is 46.6% in FY26-27 and 47.5% over 12 months, not 42.9%
verdicts.query_used: SELECT m.MOPName, COUNT(*), SUM(sp.Amount), SUM(sp.TenderAmount), SUM(sp.ReturnAmount) FROM SalePayment sp JOIN SaleHeader h ... LEFT JOIN ModeOfPayment m ... GROUP BY m.MOPName, run for FY26-27 and for 2025-09-01..2026-09-01
verdicts.why: The tender-count half — the half that actually carries the 'residents are already digital, don't build recharge' recommendation — reproduces exactly. The value half is wrong in a way neither the lane nor the vault caught. Cash rows book the full amount tendered in both Amount and TenderAmount and the change handed back in ReturnAmount; non-cash rows use Amount only. So counting cash's Amount double-counts change. Netting cash and summing Paytm.Amount + Credit.Amount + Cash.(Tender-Return) gives ₹7,65,87,017 against ₹7,66,69,025 of 12-month gross sales — a 0.11% residual. On that basis Paytm is 47.5% of value. Worth flagging upstream: Data-Quality-Traps.md Trap 3 declares every amount column unusable and 'never quote a rupee split by payment mode'. That is too strong — the split is recoverable, and the vault should be corrected.

verdicts.claim: ~36,650 bills/month in FY26-27, with 54.4% of all bills between 17:00 and 20:00
verdicts.query_used: SELECT FORMAT(VoucherDate,'yyyy-MM'), COUNT(*) FROM SaleHeader WHERE VoucherDate>='2026-04-01' GROUP BY ...; SELECT DATEPART(hour, DateTimeIn), COUNT(*) FROM SaleHeader WHERE VoucherDate>='2026-04-01' GROUP BY ...

Read literally as three hours the share is 39.7%, not 54.4%. Doesn't change the staffing recommendation.

WHERE h.VoucherDate>='2026-04-01' AND p.ProductGroupID IN (148,181,124,183,165,161) GROUP BY g.ProductGroupName

verdicts.claim: Mobile repair is unserved and ARY's entire 'Mobile' product group is 8 SKUs, all chargers — no handsets, no accessories of substance
verdicts.live_number: ProductGroupID 139 'Mobile' = 8 charger SKUs selling ₹2,690 in 12 months. The real category is 15 SKUs in ProductGroupName 'Accessories' (sub-groups Mobile Accessories / Earphone / Mobile Set) selling ₹1,98,119 in 12 months — 74x more
verdicts.query_used: ./ary assort probe mobile phone earphone headphone powerbank tempered "screen guard" usb cable adapter --months 12; then a UNION ALL comparing SUM(FinalSaleAmount) for ProductGroupID=139 against SubGroupName IN ('Mobile Accessories','Earphone','Mobile Set') over 2025-09-01..2026-09-01
verdicts.why: This is Trap 1 and the CLAUDE.md house rule verbatim: the burden of proof sits on 'missing', and probe is mandatory before any 'ARY does not carry X'. The lane read a group tag instead. Live 12-month sales: Mobile Adapter ₹49,796, Mobile Datacable ₹47,607, Bluetooth Buds ₹46,543, Mobile Ear Phone ₹39,983, Airpod ₹5,594, Bluetooth Headset ₹4,393, Bluetooth Speaker ₹1,395, plus a listed 'Mobile Handset' SKU, a 'Nokia Mobile Battery', and an 'Iphone 17 Pro Max 256Gb Silver' filed under Confectionery. The repair recommendation may still be right — repair is not the same as accessories, and I found no repair SKU anywhere — but its stated evidence is gone, and the ₹55,000/month estimate is 3.3x the entire existing mobile category's annual sales, a stretch the wrong evidence concealed.

verdicts.claim: Only ~350 named customers transact monthly and 97% of bills go to walk-in account 00001, so there is no per-resident identity to run a billed service on
verdicts.live_number: Counts reproduce (Apr 296 / May 345 / Jun 373 / Jul 432 / Aug 317; walk-in = 96.3% of bills). But named accounts carry ₹2,02,52,413 of ₹7,66,86,  — 26.5% of 12-month value at a ₹1,637 average bill, and 1,064 distinct residents transacted on a named account in 12 months
verdicts.query_used: SELECT CASE WHEN CustomerID='00001' THEN 'walk-in' ELSE 'named' END, COUNT(*), SUM(BillAmount), AVG(BillAmount) FROM SaleHeader WHERE VoucherDate>='2025-09-01' AND VoucherDate<'2026-09-01' GROUP BY ...; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID) ... WHERE CustomerID<>'00001'; SELECT ct.CustomerTypeName, COUNT(*) FROM CustomerMaster c LEFT JOIN CustomerTypeMaster ct ...
verdicts.why: The bill-count statistic is right; the conclusion drawn from it is not. By value a quarter of ARY's revenue already runs on named accounts, 1,064 distinct residents used one in the last year, and CustomerMaster's 3,514 customers are already typed (Student 3,273, Staff 107, Sponsored Students By Trust 36, Trust 20, B-Block 18). The identity rail is not a prerequisite to be built — it exists, is segmented, and carries ₹2.03 Cr/yr. That materially softens the stated blocker on both the delivery and the named-customer recommendations.

verdicts.claim: The 3,604 'Akal Academy Cs' ledger accounts are the rail for a billed service
verdicts.live_number: GroupMaster 506 = 'Akal Academy Cs', 3,604 accounts in AccountMaster
verdicts.query_used: SELECT g.GroupID, g.GroupName, COUNT(*) FROM AccountMaster a JOIN GroupMaster g ON g.GroupID=a.GroupID GROUP BY g.GroupID, g.GroupName HAVING COUNT(*)>50
verdicts.why: Exact. Reporting a near-miss of my own: I first looked in CustomerMaster, found only 3 rows matching 'Akal Academy', and nearly wrote this up as a refutation. The accounts are ledger accounts, not customer records. Same class of error as the one I am auditing — check the right table before asserting absence.

verdicts.claim: Ary Pos does 104,491 bills / ₹1.92 Cr while Ary Clothing does 4,623 bills / ₹53 L at a ₹1,146 average — so tailoring belongs at Ary Clothing
verdicts.original_number: Ary Clothing avg bill ₹1,146 vs Ary Pos ₹183
verdicts.live_number: Ary Pos 111,506 bills / ₹2,04,32,244 (₹183 avg); Ary Clothing 4,745 / ₹53,96,677 (₹1,137 avg); Basement 9 bills / ₹51,38,246. But 99.8% of stitching revenue is ALREADY billed at Ary Clothing (₹5,89,418 of ₹5,90,468 over 12 months)
verdicts.query_used: SELECT w.WarehouseName, COUNT(DISTINCT d.SerialNumber), SUM(d.FinalSaleAmount) FROM SaleDetail d JOIN SaleHeader h ... LEFT JOIN WarehouseMaster w ON w.WarehouseID=d.WarehouseID WHERE h.VoucherDate>='2026-04-01' GROUP BY w.WarehouseName; then the same restricted to ProductID='07NL' and to ProductGroupID IN (183,124,165)
verdicts.why: Every figure reproduces, including the Basement wholesale anomaly. But the recommendation drawn from it — 'tailoring and alteration belong at Ary Clothing' — is already the status quo and therefore a no-op. The live finding the lane should have drawn from its own table is the inverse: fabric and unstitched suits split almost evenly between the two counters (Ary Clothing ₹21.6 L, Ary Pos ₹20.7 L over 12 months), yet Ary Pos books 4 stitching lines a year. Half of ARY's fabric is sold at a counter with no stitching desk.

verdicts.claim: Tailors are settled up — net payable to all 18 is -₹3,388 — so the thin margin is not a timing artefact
verdicts.live_number: -₹3,388 exactly (credits ₹17,02,929, debits ₹17,06,317). But the last stitching accrual is dated 31-Jul-2026 and August's ₹43,410 of stitching revenue has no cost booked against it
verdicts.query_used: SELECT SUM(c.CreditAmount)-SUM(c.DebitAmount) FROM TransactionChild c JOIN TransactionMaster m ON m.SerialNumber=c.SerialNumber JOIN AccountMaster a ON a.AccountID=c.AccountID WHERE a.GroupID=508 AND m.IsDeleted=0; plus the monthly expense series
verdicts.why: The number is exact to the rupee. The inference is not: the payable is flat precisely because the cost is accrued by a single month-end journal, so it is always near zero on the last accrual date and always understated after it. It removes the WIP objection for July and earlier and says nothing about August. This is the same cut-off that inflates the headline margin.

verdicts.claim: The recommended service set contributes ~₹2.0-2.2 L/month, about 2.8% of ARY's ~₹8.96 Cr annualised revenue
verdicts.live_number: The sizing table's contribution column sums to ₹2,24,000/month. Trailing 12-month gross sales are ₹7,66,69,025 and net of ₹17,08,858 of returns are ₹7,49,60,166 — so the share is ~3.0-3.6%, not 2.8%
verdicts.query_used: SELECT SUM(d.FinalSaleAmount) FROM SaleDetail d JOIN SaleHeader h ... WHERE h.VoucherDate>='2025-09-01' AND h.VoucherDate<'2026-09-01'; SELECT SUM(r.FinalSaleAmount) FROM SaleReturnDetail r JOIN SaleReturnHeader rh ...; plus arithmetic on the lane's own table
verdicts.why: Three separate problems, none fatal but all in the same direction. (1) The table sums to ₹2.24 L, above the stated range. (2) ₹8.96 Cr annualises the Apr-Aug peak, which includes the school session start; the actual trailing year is ₹7.50 Cr net, so the denominator is ~19% too big. (3) More seriously, the portfolio's blended contribution margin is ₹2.24 L on ₹4.15 L of revenue = 54%, with no labour deducted in any row — even though the print row lists '1 operator' as a requirement and the lane's own recommendation is that the counter be staffed 17:00-20:00. One salary at Baru Sahib rates would consume a quarter of the whole portfolio's contribution. The lane's own honesty caveat ('services will not move ARY's top line much') is the right conclusion; the number reaching it is soft.

verdicts.claim: India Post franchise commission rates and NPCI's AePS interchange could not be verified
verdicts.live_number: n/a
verdicts.query_used: none — the lane states no figure to test
verdicts.why: Correctly marked NOT-CHECKED, with the failed URLs and the absent Wayback snapshots named. No number is asserted and no recommendation rests on one; the courier case is explicitly rebuilt on a private-carrier model instead. This is how an unverifiable external should be handled, and the same discipline shows in the CSC finding, where the lane flags that its own source pages date to 2016-17 and that HP is not a Digital Seva e-District state. Separately, I confirmed the Wikipedia figures the print sizing leans on (1,538 students, 24 programmes, 129 schools, ~60,000 students, 400 acres in 1956) are all present verbatim on that page — though a Wikipedia number carries no date and should not be treated as a current headcount.
